items.title: Section: Why Alcohol Gets Its Own Branch, and How Every Lesser Ordination Nests Within the Monastic and Lay Categories

items.zh: 遠離諸酒眾放逸處，是第五支。何以故？彼雖安住正憶念支，謂我今住決定齋戒。若為諸酒所醉，便發狂亂，不自在轉。今於此中，若苾芻尼律儀，若正學、勤策、勤策女律儀，皆在出家品所攝故，當知攝屬苾芻律儀。若近事女律儀，墮在家品故，相似學所顯故，當知攝屬近事律儀。問：何故世尊於苾芻律儀中制立苾芻、勤策二眾律儀，於苾芻尼律儀中制立苾芻尼、正學、勤策女三眾律儀。答：由彼母邑多煩惱故，令漸受學苾芻尼律儀。
items.en:
Fifth, the fifth branch; first, stating it. Abstaining from intoxicants and the occasions for heedlessness is the fifth branch. Second, the question raised. Why is this so? Third, the explanation. Even while abiding in this branch of settled mindfulness, resolved on this observance, one overcome by intoxicants becomes deranged, losing self-command.
Second, showing how the rest are subsumed; first, subsumed under monastic restraint. Here, the precepts of a fully ordained nun, a probationary nun, a novice monk, and a novice nun are all subsumed under the category of leaving household life, and should be known as subsumed under monastic restraint.
Second, subsumed under lay restraint. The precepts of a laywoman, falling under the household category and revealed as resembling monastic training in reduced form, should be known as subsumed under lay restraint.
Second, resolving objections; first, the objection regarding two versus three categories; first, the question. Question: why did the Blessed One establish only two categories — full monastic and novice — within monastic restraint, yet three categories — full monastic, probationary, and novice — within the restraint of nuns?
Second, the answer; first, stating the reason. Answer: because women are generally more susceptible to affliction, they are led to undertake the nuns' restraint gradually.

items.title: Section: A Gradual Path to Full Ordination — And Why Novices Alone Are Forbidden to Handle Money

items.zh: 若於勤策女少分學處深生喜樂，次應授彼正學所有學處。若於正學多分學處深生愛樂，不應率爾授彼具足，必更二年久處習學，若深愛樂，然後當授彼具足戒。如是長時於少學處積修學已，次方有力能受廣大眾多學處，然後於苾芻尼律儀能具修學。問：何故於勤策律儀中增離金銀，非於近住律儀耶？答：由彼勤策在出家眾攝。夫出家者，於二種處極非淨妙。一者、墮欲樂邊，嬉戲、嚴身、所行、所受皆隨所樂。二者、蓄積財寶。為除斷初非淨妙處，施設遠離歌舞伎樂乃至非時而食。
items.en:
Second, explaining the appropriate progression. Whoever takes deep delight in the novice nun's training rules, a lesser portion of the renunciant precepts, should next be given the probationary precepts. Whoever takes deep delight in the probationary training rules, the greater portion, should not hastily be given full ordination, but must undergo a further two years of practice; only once this delight has proven durable should full ordination then be conferred.
Third, clarifying the gradual sequence. Only through long accumulated practice within lesser training rules does one gain the capacity to undertake far more extensive rules, and only then can full training in the nun's precepts be completed.
Second, the objection regarding the added prohibition on gold and silver; first, the question. Question: why does novice restraint add abstinence from gold and silver, while the one-day precepts do not?
Second, the answer; first, stating what novice restraint belongs to. Answer: because novice restraint belongs to the category of renunciation. Second, revealing the two unclean matters; first, stating them. A renunciant faces two matters that are especially unclean; second, listing them. First, falling into sensory pleasure — amusement, adornment, and conduct pursued according to one's own enjoyment; second, accumulating wealth.
Third, clarifying their establishment; first, addressing the first matter. To eliminate the first unclean matter, abstinence from song and dance up through eating after midday was established.

items.title: Section: Why Gold and Silver Specifically Are Forbidden, and the Tree-Spirit Who Shamed a Discouraged Monk Back to practise

items.zh: 為斷第二非淨妙處，施設遠離執受金銀。由彼金銀一切財寶之根本故，又最勝故。
items.en: Second, addressing the second unclean matter; first, stating it. To eliminate this second unclean matter, abstinence from handling gold and silver was established. Second, explaining why. Because gold and silver are the root of all material wealth, and its most concentrated form.

items.title: Section: One Combined Precept for a Single Day, Two Separate Ones for a Lifetime — Matching the Rule to the Commitment

items.zh: 問：何故於勤策律儀中，遠離歌舞伎樂及塗冠香鬘制立二支，於近住律儀中合為一支耶？答：諸在家者於此處所非不如法，諸出家者極不如法。是故於在家者，就輕總制為一學處。云何令彼若暫違犯，尋自懇責，合一發露，不由二種。諸出家者，於此一處就重別制以為兩支。云何令彼若起違犯，便自懇責，二種發露，不但由一。
items.en:
Third, the objection regarding combining or separating this precept; first, the question. Question: why does novice restraint establish abstinence from entertainment and from adornment as two separate precepts, while the one-day precepts combine them into one?
Second, the answer; first, stating the distinction. Answer: for householders, these matters are not improper in themselves; for renunciants, they are profoundly improper.
Second, explaining the combining and separating; first, regarding householders. Therefore, for householders, treated as a lighter matter, these are combined into a single training rule, so that a momentary lapse may be addressed with a single act of self-reproach and confession, not two.
Second, regarding renunciants. For renunciants, treated as a weightier matter here, these are established separately as two distinct precepts, so that any lapse requires two separate acts of self-reproach and confession, not merely one.

items.title: Section: Who Cannot Be Ordained — Three Reasons the Treatise Gives for Excluding Certain Individuals from Monastic Life

items.zh: 問：何故不許扇搋迦、半擇迦出家及受具足戒耶？答：由此二種，若置苾芻眾中，便參女過；若置苾芻尼眾中，因摩觸等，便參男過。由不應與二眾共居，是故不許此類出家及受具足。又由此二煩惱多故，性煩惱障極覆障故，不能發起如是思擇。彼尚不能思擇，思擇令其戒蘊清淨現行，何況當證勝過人法。是故不許彼類出家及受具戒。又彼眾中好人難得，亦難觀察。
items.en:
Fourth, the objection regarding two categories not being accommodated; first, why ordination is not permitted; first, the question. Question: why are the ṣaṇḍhaka and the paṇḍaka not permitted to leave household life or receive full ordination?
Second, the answer; first, through introducing two kinds of impropriety. Answer: placed among the community of monks, such a one would introduce the impropriety associated with a woman; placed among the community of nuns, incidental contact would introduce the impropriety associated with a man. Since neither community could appropriately house such a person, ordination is not permitted.
Second, through lacking the capacity for reflection. Furthermore, since such individuals carry an unusually heavy affliction obstruction, so thoroughly obscured that they cannot even properly reflect on keeping their own precepts pure, still less attain anything transcending the ordinary human condition — for this reason, ordination is not permitted.
Third, through the difficulty of evaluation. Furthermore, within this group good people are rare and difficult to discern.

items.title: Section: Equal Merit Despite Unequal Titles — And the Third Category, Ordinary Conduct Belonging to Neither Vow

items.zh: 二雖受歸依，亦能隨受諸近事男所有學處，而不得名近事男耶？答：近事男者，名能親近承事苾芻、苾芻尼眾。彼雖能護所受律儀，而不應數親近承事苾芻、苾芻尼眾。苾芻、苾芻尼等亦復不應親近攝受，若摩、若觸如是種類，又亦不應如近事男而相親善。是故彼類不得名近事男。然其受護所有學處，當知福德等無差別。復次，云何非律儀非不律儀？謂除如先所說律儀、不律儀業，所有善不善等身語意業，當知一切皆是非律儀非不律儀業所攝。問：諸有律儀，若由自受、若由他受、若從他受、若自然受，如是所受律儀所獲福德，為有勝劣差別不耶？答：若等心受，亦如是持，當知無有差別。
items.en:
Second, revealing the equal merit involved. Yet the merit generated by receiving and guarding these training precepts should be known as entirely equal.
Third, subsumed under neither vow; first, the question posed. Furthermore, what is conduct belonging to neither an unwholesome nor a wholesome vow?
Second, the explanation. Apart from everything already described under either vow, every other wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral action of body, speech, and mind should be known as subsumed under this third category.
Second, a question-and-answer analysis; first, distinguishing the merit involved; first, the question. Question: among all who hold precepts — whether received through oneself, through another's urging, through a preceptor, or spontaneously — is the merit generated superior or inferior depending on how it was received?
Second, the answer. Answer: whoever receives with an equally sincere mind, and likewise sustains it with equal diligence, generates entirely equal merit, one should know.

blocks.text: Why alcohol has its own precept, why novices may not handle gold and silver, and the assurance that merit depends on the heart, not the title.
One may be resolved on the observance, yet "if overcome by intoxicants, becomes deranged and loses self-command". Master Cháng Bǎi: drinking can destroy right mindfulness.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the novice's rules are a small part of the full monastic code.

Novices belong to the renunciant community, for whom two things are especially unclean: falling into sensual pleasure and accumulating wealth. To cut the second, handling gold and silver was forbidden.
These matters are not improper for householders, but very improper for renunciants. Master Cháng Bǎi: for lay followers, two branches are combined into one training rule.
Three reasons: such a person could not live properly in either community; heavy affliction prevents the reflection that keeps precepts pure; and good people among them are hard to find.

"The merit of receiving and guarding these training precepts is entirely equal." Whoever receives with an equal mind and sustains it likewise generates no difference. The third category, belonging to neither vow, covers every other action. Master Cháng Bǎi: most ordinary people are of neither vow, doing good or evil as conditions arise.
"Equal merit, however received." The form of a vow differs; the sincerity behind it is what counts.

quiz.q: Why is abstaining from intoxicants set apart as the branch of not destroying mindfulness?
options: drinking is a natural offence graver than killing, so it stands alone
though abiding in recollection, one who gets drunk becomes deranged; drinking destroys right mindfulness
alcohol is forbidden only on observance days and not at other times, so it is set apart from lifelong rules
alcohol is a food belonging to untimely meals, so it is set apart
quiz.why: The treatise reasons that one may be abiding in the branch of recollection, resolved on the observance, yet if overcome by intoxicants becomes deranged and loses self-command. Master Cháng Bǎi: drinking can destroy right mindfulness, and so abstaining from it falls under the branch of not destroying mindfulness.

quiz.q: The English has "they are led to undertake monastic restraint gradually" for 令漸受學苾芻尼律儀. What is the problem?
options: the Chinese says the nuns' restraint, while "monastic restraint" here renders the monks', so the English is inexact
the Chinese says novice restraint, so "monastic" is wrong
the Chinese has no word for gradually, so it is an addition to delete
the Chinese says women cannot receive the precepts at all, and the English turns this into an affirmative, reversing it
quiz.why: The Chinese says 苾芻尼律儀, the nuns' restraint. In this passage the English uses "monastic restraint" for the monks' and "the restraint of nuns" for the nuns', so its sentence names the wrong one. Master Cháng Bǎi: only when a trainee nun can keep a few rules does she gain the capacity to undertake the many and extensive training rules.

quiz.q: The English has "even a portion of the novice nun's training rules" for 勤策女少分學處. According to the lecture, what does 少分 mean?
options: a novice nun need learn only a few of the ten rules and may leave the others until full ordination
少分 means a short training time, of only one year
少分 means novice nuns are few, so they must be strictly chosen
the novice nun's rules are a small part of monastic rules as a whole, not a part of the novice nun's own rules
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if one takes deep delight in the novice nun's precepts, which are a small part of the monastics' rules. So 少分 describes the novice's rules in relation to the full code, not a part of them. The English "a portion of the novice nun's training rules" suggests she keeps only some of her own rules, and the "greater part" of the next line has the same problem.

quiz.q: Why does novice restraint add abstinence from gold and silver, while the one-day precepts do not?
options: novices are young and easily tempted, while one-day observers are mostly elders
novices belong to renunciants, who must cut off sensory pleasure and hoarded wealth; gold and silver are the root of wealth
one-day observers must make offerings, so they need to hold gold and silver
in the Buddha's day only renunciants could obtain gold and silver
quiz.why: The treatise answers that novices belong to the renunciant community, for whom two matters are especially unclean: falling into sensory pleasure and accumulating wealth. To cut the second, abstinence from handling gold and silver was established. Master Cháng Bǎi: gold and silver are the root of all wealth and its most valuable form, and they easily stir a practitioner's greed.

quiz.q: Why are entertainment and adornment two precepts for novices but one for the one-day precepts?
options: for householders they are very improper, so they are combined as weightier; for renunciants not improper, so they are separated as lighter
the one-day observance is too short to keep two rules
for householders these are not improper, so the lighter treatment combines them; for renunciants they are very improper, so they are separated
the novice's ten must total ten and the one-day eight must total eight
quiz.why: The treatise says these matters are not improper for householders, but very improper for renunciants. Master Cháng Bǎi: for lay followers the lighter treatment makes the two branches one training rule; a renunciant who transgresses must reproach himself and confess two offenses, not only one. The practical result is a difference in how a lapse is confessed.

quiz.q: What three reasons does the treatise give for not permitting this group to ordain?
options: they fit neither community without impropriety; heavy affliction prevents reflection; good people among them are rare and hard to discern
weak bodies unfit for alms-rounds, uncertain lifespan, and inability to study
worldly criticism, parental refusal, and official prohibition
low lineage, evil karma of past lives, and no spiritual friends
quiz.why: The treatise gives three reasons: such a person could not properly live in either community; heavy affliction prevents the reflection that keeps the precepts pure, still less the attainment beyond it; and good people among them are hard to find and hard to discern. Master Cháng Bǎi on the second: the afflictive obstruction is so great that they cannot reflect in this way or attain a renunciant's fruit.

quiz.q: The English has "genuinely good character is said to be rare" for 好人難得. How does it differ from the Chinese?
options: the Chinese says there are no good people at all, so "rare" softens it
the Chinese states it directly, with no "said to be"; it speaks of few good people in this group, not of "character"
the Chinese says good people are many, so "rare" reverses it
the Chinese says a good teacher is rare, and the English changes the subject
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: among such people good people are few, and it is not easy to see who is a good person. The treatise states this directly, whereas the English "is said to be" turns it into hearsay, and "good character" moves from persons to a quality. The softening is the translator's and should be marked, not attributed to the text.

quiz.q: Though such people may not ordain or be called lay devotees, how does their merit in keeping precepts compare, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: their merit is half a lay devotee's, because the vow's basis is incomplete and they cannot attend on monastics
they have no merit at all, since they may not receive precepts
their merit does not differ from a lay devotee's; they simply cannot attend on the community and so lack the name
their merit exceeds a lay devotee's, because their practice is harder
quiz.why: The treatise says the merit of receiving and guarding these training precepts is entirely equal. Master Cháng Bǎi: the merit gained does not differ from a lay devotee's; it is only that they cannot attend on monks and nuns or come into the community, and so they are not called by that name. The title depends on the role, not on the merit.

quiz.q: What sort of person belongs to "neither vow," according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: only noble śrāvakas, who have gone beyond keeping and not keeping, and no longer act as conditions arise
most ordinary people, who do evil or good as conditions arise, without a strong wish for release
only butchers and hunters, who live by killing
only those whose one-day precepts have ended at sunrise
quiz.why: The treatise defines this category by exclusion: every other wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral action of body, speech, and mind. Master Cháng Bǎi: most ordinary people are of neither vow, often doing evil or good as conditions arise; they have no strong wish for release, and doing good is simply doing good. One of unwholesome vow, by contrast, has a strong resolve.

quiz.q: Does merit differ with the manner of receiving the precepts? How does the treatise answer?
options: reception through another is superior, having a teacher to witness it and a community to support it
whoever receives with an equal mind and sustains likewise has no difference of merit
spontaneous reception is superior, arising wholly from oneself
reception at another's urging is lowest, not arising from oneself
quiz.why: Asked whether merit is superior or inferior according to how the precepts were received, the treatise answers that whoever receives with an equal mind and likewise sustains it generates no difference. Master Cháng Bǎi: given equal resolve, the merit gained is equal. The deciding factor is the mind in receiving and keeping, not the outward mode.
